subject.title: [Bug]: codex harness mirrored-session-history read fails for ephemeral sessions and on failover; one-shot cleanup retires shared app-server client while turns are in flight

question: Should maintainers repair this as one Codex harness/session-state issue, or split https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99575 as a narrow missing-file warning fix while separately owning Codex `session_meta`, shared-client lifecycle, and fallback transcript continuity?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the durable fix crosses plugin-owned Codex rollout parsing, Active Memory one-shot lifecycle, and cross-provider fallback transcript semantics, so automation should not choose the product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Own one scoped harness repair
options.body: Treat `session_meta` handling, safe one-shot client lifecycle, and fallback transcript continuity as one maintainer-scoped Codex harness repair plan before reopening fix automation.

options.title: Land the warning-only PR first
options.body: Review and potentially land https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/99575 as a narrow ENOENT warning cleanup while keeping this issue open for the remaining runtime and failover behavior.

options.title: Split into separate canonical issues
options.body: Make Active Memory timeout, shared-client retirement, and fallback transcript recovery separate tracked items if maintainers want smaller owner boundaries.

recommendation.title: Own one scoped harness repair
recommendation.body: Treat `session_meta` handling, safe one-shot client lifecycle, and fallback transcript continuity as one maintainer-scoped Codex harness repair plan before reopening fix automation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal is the transcript mirror refactor that owns the implicated session-history and attempt-context integration surface.
